doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

title: Securing the archive's future under Monk Rowe
summary: Fillius says musicians know Rowe as Hamilton College, and wants the archive made secure.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well the people we’ve dealt with have a talent. They’ve all got a God-given talent, and that makes them different. I look at guys like Haggart and Ralph Sutton and guys like that who were drunks when they were young. They more than drank their share. But the guys who made it got smart and got off that stuff, and are the ones who have lasted, the ones that we’re dealing with have all wised up from that. They’ve had that experience. And they make wonderful friends, they really do. And I’m very attached to a lot of them. And so is Nikki. Nikki and Sharon Rosengarden are like sisters. They call each other sisters. But I think, I know that you’ve done a great job and I’m damned if I’m not going to be sure that you stay on here. Because that’s the key really. Because the musicians all know you now. You’re Hamilton College. I’m not. It’s amazing.
Well I could argue about that.

No, no, really, no. I go to some place and say something about Hamilton and they’ll look at me and say, “Isn’t that where Monk Rowe is?” I say, “Yeah, that’s where Monk Rowe is.” Or, “Isn’t that Monk’s College?” No that’s right and that’s fine because you’re the queen bee around which all this operates. My desire, as of yesterday too, is to try to get this thing on a basis where you’re safe and secure and the thing is okay to go on. Well for the public, I won’t say any more about it but you know what I mean.
